title: Cornelius the centurion + Peter's vision of the sheet: the Spirit poured out on the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Now [there was] a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of the band called the Italian [band],
paragraphs.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος, ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς,
paragraphs.translit: Anēr de tis en Kaisareia onomati Kornēlios, hekatontarchēs ek speirēs tēs kaloumenēs Italikēs,

paragraphs.text: a devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, who gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God always.
paragraphs.original: εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ παντός,
paragraphs.translit: eusebēs kai phoboumenos ton theon syn panti tō oikō autou, poiōn eleēmosynas pollas tō laō kai deomenos tou theou dia pantos,

paragraphs.text: He saw in a vision openly, as it were about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in unto him, and saying to him, Cornelius.
paragraphs.original: εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς ὡσεὶ περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ· Κορνήλιε.
paragraphs.translit: eiden en horamati phanerōs hōsei peri hōran enatēn tēs hēmeras angelon tou theou eiselthonta pros auton kai eiponta autō· Kornēlie.

paragraphs.text: And he, fastening his eyes upon him, and being affrighted, said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are gone up for a memorial before God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν· Τί ἐστιν, κύριε; εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ho de atenisas autō kai emphobos genomenos eipen· Ti estin, kyrie; eipen de autō· Hai proseuchai sou kai hai eleēmosynai sou anebēsan eis mnēmosynon emprosthen tou theou·

paragraphs.text: And now send men to Joppa, and fetch one Simon, who is surnamed Peter:
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος·
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn pempson andras eis Ioppēn kai metapempsai Simōna tina hos epikaleitai Petros·

paragraphs.text: he lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ, ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: houtos xenizetai para tini Simōni byrsei, hō estin oikia para thalassan.

paragraphs.text: And when the angel that spake unto him was departed, he called two of his household-servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν αὐτῷ, φωνήσας δύο τῶν οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ
paragraphs.translit: hōs de apēlthen ho angelos ho lalōn autō, phōnēsas dyo tōn oiketōn kai stratiōtēn eusebē tōn proskarterountōn autō

paragraphs.text: and having rehearsed all things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην.
paragraphs.translit: kai exēgēsamenos hapanta autois apesteilen autous eis tēn Ioppēn.

paragraphs.text: Now on the morrow, as they were on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour:
paragraphs.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην.
paragraphs.translit: Tē de epaurion hodoiporountōn ekeinōn kai tē polei engizontōn anebē Petros epi to dōma proseuxasthai peri hōran hektēn.

paragraphs.text: and he became hungry, and desired to eat: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance;
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι· παρασκευαζόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐγένετο ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις,
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de prospeinos kai ēthelen geusasthai· paraskeuazontōn de autōn egeneto epʼ auton ekstasis,

paragraphs.text: and he beholdeth the heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet, let down by four corners upon the earth:
paragraphs.original: καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
paragraphs.translit: kai theōrei ton ouranon aneōgmenon kai katabainon skeuos ti hōs othonēn megalēn tessarsin archais kathiemenon epi tēs gēs,

paragraphs.text: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts and creeping things of the earth and birds of the heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: en hō hypērchen panta ta tetrapoda kai herpeta tēs gēs kai peteina tou ouranou.

paragraphs.text: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto phōnē pros auton· Anastas, Petre, thyson kai phage.

paragraphs.text: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common and unclean.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros eipen· Mēdamōs, kyrie, hoti oudepote ephagon pan koinon kai akatharton.

paragraphs.text: And a voice [came] unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai phōnē palin ek deuterou pros auton· Ha ho theos ekatharisen sy mē koinou.

paragraphs.text: And this was done thrice: and straightway the vessel was received up into heaven.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de egeneto epi tris, kai euthys anelēmphthē to skeuos eis ton ouranon.

paragraphs.text: Now while Peter was much perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men that were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon`s house, stood before the gate,
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν, ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα,
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de en heautō diēporei ho Petros ti an eiē to horama ho eiden, idou hoi andres hoi apestalmenoi hypo tou Kornēliou dierōtēsantes tēn oikian tou Simōnos epestēsan epi ton pylōna,

paragraphs.text: and called and asked whether Simon, who was surnamed Peter, were lodging there.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φωνήσαντες ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai phōnēsantes epynthanonto ei Simōn ho epikaloumenos Petros enthade xenizetai.

paragraphs.text: And while Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.
paragraphs.original: τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ πνεῦμα· Ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες ζητοῦντές σε·
paragraphs.translit: tou de Petrou dienthymoumenou peri tou horamatos eipen autō to pneuma· Idou andres zētountes se·

paragraphs.text: But arise, and get thee down, and go with them, nothing doubting: for I have sent them.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: alla anastas katabēthi kai poreuou syn autois mēden diakrinomenos, hoti egō apestalka autous.

paragraphs.text: And Peter went down to the men, and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?
paragraphs.original: καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία διʼ ἣν πάρεστε;
paragraphs.translit: katabas de Petros pros tous andras eipen· Idou egō eimi hon zēteite· tis hē aitia diʼ hēn pareste;

paragraphs.text: And they said, Cornelius a centurion, a righteous man and one that feareth God, and well reported of by all the nation of the Jews, was warned [of God] by a holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words from thee.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan· Kornēlios hekatontarchēs, anēr dikaios kai phoboumenos ton theon martyroumenos te hypo holou tou ethnous tōn Ioudaiōn, echrēmatisthē hypo angelou hagiou metapempsasthai se eis ton oikon autou kai akousai rhēmata para sou.

paragraphs.text: So he called them in and lodged them. And on the morrow he arose and went forth with them, and certain of the brethren from Joppa accompanied him.
paragraphs.original: εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν. Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς, καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: eiskalesamenos oun autous exenisen. Tē de epaurion anastas exēlthen syn autois, kai tines tōn adelphōn tōn apo Ioppēs synēlthon autō.

paragraphs.text: And on the morrow they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his kinsmen and his near friends.
paragraphs.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν. ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους.
paragraphs.translit: tē de epaurion eisēlthen eis tēn Kaisareian. ho de Kornēlios ēn prosdokōn autous synkalesamenos tous syngeneis autou kai tous anankaious philous.

paragraphs.text: And when it came to pass that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον, συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de egeneto tou eiselthein ton Petron, synantēsas autō ho Kornēlios pesōn epi tous podas prosekynēsen.

paragraphs.text: But Peter raised him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι· καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros ēgeiren auton legōn· Anastēthi· kai egō autos anthrōpos eimi.

paragraphs.text: And as he talked with him, he went in, and findeth many come together:
paragraphs.original: καὶ συνομιλῶν αὐτῷ εἰσῆλθεν, καὶ εὑρίσκει συνεληλυθότας πολλούς,
paragraphs.translit: kai synomilōn autō eisēlthen, kai heuriskei synelēlythotas pollous,

paragraphs.text: and he said unto them, Ye yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to join himself or come unto one of another nation; and [yet] unto me hath God showed that I should not call any man common or unclean:
paragraphs.original: ἔφη τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὡς ἀθέμιτόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ Ἰουδαίῳ κολλᾶσθαι ἢ προσέρχεσθαι ἀλλοφύλῳ· κἀμοὶ ὁ θεὸς ἔδειξεν μηδένα κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον λέγειν ἄνθρωπον·
paragraphs.translit: ephē te pros autous· Hymeis epistasthe hōs athemiton estin andri Ioudaiō kollasthai ē proserchesthai allophylō· kamoi ho theos edeixen mēdena koinon ē akatharton legein anthrōpon·

paragraphs.text: wherefore also I came without gainsaying, when I was sent for. I ask therefore with what intent ye sent for me.
paragraphs.original: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς. πυνθάνομαι οὖν τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με.
paragraphs.translit: dio kai anantirrētōs ēlthon metapemphtheis. pynthanomai oun tini logō metepempsasthe me.

paragraphs.text: And Cornelius said, Four days ago, until this hour, I was keeping the ninth hour of prayer in my house; and behold, a man stood before me in bright apparel,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη· Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ἤμην τὴν ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ
paragraphs.translit: Kai ho Kornēlios ephē· Apo tetartēs hēmeras mechri tautēs tēs hōras ēmēn tēn enatēn proseuchomenos en tō oikō mou, kai idou anēr estē enōpion mou en esthēti lampra

paragraphs.text: and saith, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φησί· Κορνήλιε, εἰσηκούσθη σου ἡ προσευχὴ καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai phēsi· Kornēlie, eisēkousthē sou hē proseuchē kai hai eleēmosynai sou emnēsthēsan enōpion tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Send therefore to Joppa, and call unto thee Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he lodgeth in the house of Simon a tanner, by the sea side.
paragraphs.original: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος· οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: pempson oun eis Ioppēn kai metakalesai Simōna hos epikaleitai Petros· houtos xenizetai en oikia Simōnos byrseōs para thalassan.

paragraphs.text: Forthwith therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God, to hear all things that have been commanded thee of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος. νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: exautēs oun epempsa pros se, sy te kalōs epoiēsas paragenomenos. nyn oun pantes hēmeis enōpion tou theou paresmen akousai panta ta prostetagmena soi hypo tou kyriou.

paragraphs.text: And Peter opened his mouth and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
paragraphs.original: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός,
paragraphs.translit: Anoixas de Petros to stoma eipen· Epʼ alētheias katalambanomai hoti ouk estin prosōpolēmptēs ho theos,

paragraphs.text: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is acceptable to him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ en panti ethnei ho phoboumenos auton kai ergazomenos dikaiosynēn dektos autō estin.

paragraphs.text: The word which he sent unto the children of Israel, preaching good tidings of peace by Jesus Christ (He is Lord of all.) --
paragraphs.original: τὸν λόγον ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων κύριος.
paragraphs.translit: ton logon hon apesteilen tois hyiois Israēl euangelizomenos eirēnēn dia Iēsou Christou· houtos estin pantōn kyrios.

paragraphs.text: that saying ye yourselves know, which was published throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης,
paragraphs.translit: hymeis oidate to genomenon rhēma kathʼ holēs tēs Ioudaias, arxamenos apo tēs Galilaias meta to baptisma ho ekēryxen Iōannēs,

paragraphs.text: [even] Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.
paragraphs.original: Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Iēsoun ton apo Nazareth, hōs echrisen auton ho theos pneumati hagiō kai dynamei, hos diēlthen euergetōn kai iōmenos pantas tous katadynasteuomenous hypo tou diabolou, hoti ho theos ēn metʼ autou·

paragraphs.text: And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom also they slew, hanging him on a tree.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēmeis martyres pantōn hōn epoiēsen en te tē chōra tōn Ioudaiōn kai Ierousalēm· hon kai aneilan kremasantes epi xylou.

paragraphs.text: Him God raised up the third day, and gave him to be made manifest,
paragraphs.original: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι,
paragraphs.translit: touton ho theos ēgeiren tē tritē hēmera kai edōken auton emphanē genesthai,

paragraphs.text: not to all the people, but unto witnesses that were chosen before of God, [even] to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
paragraphs.original: οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσι τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ou panti tō laō alla martysi tois prokecheirotonēmenois hypo tou theou, hēmin, hoitines synephagomen kai synepiomen autō meta to anastēnai auton ek nekrōn·

paragraphs.text: And he charged us to preach unto the people, and to testify that this is he who is ordained of God [to be] the Judge of the living and the dead.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai parēngeilen hēmin kēryxai tō laō kai diamartyrasthai hoti houtos estin ho hōrismenos hypo tou theou kritēs zōntōn kai nekrōn.

paragraphs.text: To him bear all the prophets witness, that through his name every one that believeth on him shall receive remission of sins.
paragraphs.original: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: toutō pantes hoi prophētai martyrousin, aphesin hamartiōn labein dia tou onomatos autou panta ton pisteuonta eis auton.

paragraphs.text: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all them that heard the word.
paragraphs.original: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.
paragraphs.translit: Eti lalountos tou Petrou ta rhēmata tauta epepese to pneuma to hagion epi pantas tous akouontas ton logon.

paragraphs.text: And they of the circumcision that believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται·
paragraphs.translit: kai exestēsan hoi ek peritomēs pistoi hosoi synēlthan tō Petrō, hoti kai epi ta ethnē hē dōrea tou hagiou pneumatos ekkechytai·

paragraphs.text: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
paragraphs.original: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν. τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·
paragraphs.translit: ēkouon gar autōn lalountōn glōssais kai megalynontōn ton theon. tote apekrithē Petros·

paragraphs.text: Can any man forbid the water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?
paragraphs.original: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: Mēti to hydōr dynatai kōlysai tis tou mē baptisthēnai toutous hoitines to pneuma to hagion elabon hōs kai hēmeis;

paragraphs.text: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
paragraphs.original: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι. τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.
paragraphs.translit: prosetaxen de autous en tō onomati Iēsou Christou baptisthēnai. tote ērōtēsan auton epimeinai hēmeras tinas.
